habit_scope: Wood / vinyl / hardboard siding over WRB on 2-story light-wood SFR. AF&PA Exterior Siding + CMHC Ch13. Stucco, masonry veneer, EIFS are alts not this habit. Roof finish is m-P11-asphalt-shingles-finish. Can overlap P12 and P14 — no lag days invented.
how_it_is_done: WRB and window flashing already in (P10). CMHC Ch2: exterior finishes (masonry, siding, stucco, soffit, fascia, eavestroughs, downspouts, caulking and flashing of windows and doors) after insulation may run at the same time as insulation IF the insulated assembly is protected from wind-driven rain. Can overlap MEP rough and drywall. No lag days invented.
AF&PA (US): siding and exterior trim over Type 15 asphalt felt or other water-repellent sheathing cover, corrosion-resistant nails (hot-dipped galvanized, stainless, or aluminum).

Nail length AF&PA: for smooth-shank siding nails, combined siding+sheathing thickness PLUS 1-1/2 in into solid wood. Foam/insulation-board sheathing: 1-1/2 in into the stud. Plywood/OSB/waferboard thickness counts toward that 1-1/2 in. Ring/spiral shank: 1/8 to 1/4 in less penetration permitted.

Bevel / square-edge horizontal: one nail at each stud; min 1 in lap; nail about 1-1/2 in above the lap (AF&PA Fig 68a). Drop/shiplap flush to paper: one nail at each stud about 1-1/2 in above the drip edge; two nails if width ≥8 in or sheathing omitted (Fig 68b).
Vertical board: nails 16 in vertically over ≥1/2 in wood/plywood/structural panel sheathing; otherwise 1x4 furring at 24 in as nail base. Studs >16 in: 2-in lumber blocking between studs (AF&PA).

CMHC lumber siding (CANADIAN — confirm AHJ): corrosion-resistant / hot-dipped galvanized; casing or siding nails; heads flush; finish nails set and filled. Nail long enough to penetrate at least 25 mm (1 in) into the nailing support. Bevel: 6 mm (1/4 in) furring under the bottom course; overlap each course at least 25 mm (1 in). Nail just above the lap so the nail misses the top edge of the piece beneath (Fig 111). T&G: first board face-nailed near groove, angle-nailed through tongue; successive boards fitted tight and angle-nailed through the tongue. Vinyl/metal: nails in the center of the slots, not hammered tight, so the siding can move. Laps of adjacent strips staggered more than 600 mm (24 in).

Grade clearance: AF&PA Fig 54 — 6 in min siding to finished grade (US book). CMHC — most siding ≥200 mm (8 in) from ground and ≥50 mm (2 in) from an adjoining roof surface — CANADIAN. Do not copy 8 in as Utah/Fontana without AHJ.
Corners: AF&PA Fig 69 / CMHC Fig 112 — corner boards, mitred, metal covers, or lapped. Protect ends at corners, butts, and window/door trim with clear water-repellent preservative (AF&PA).
Rainscreen/furring: CMHC requires strapping in wet humid coastal climates. Not a Utah/Fontana habit unless AHJ says so. Do not invent a Fontana rainscreen.
Stucco, masonry veneer, EIFS are named alts (m-P11-stucco, m-P11-masonry-veneer, m-P11-eifs). Do not shop EIFS as first-touch.
tools_equipment: Named: corrosion-resistant siding nails; nail set; furring. Not a SKU list.

Siding nails miss the course below (AF&PA 1-1/2 in above lap; CMHC Fig 111).

Vinyl/metal: nails in slot centers, not driven tight (CMHC).
Exterior finishes may overlap insulation only if the assembly is protected from wind-driven rain (CMHC Ch2).
material_classes: corrosion-resistant siding nails (hot-dipped galvanized / stainless / aluminum)
ring-shank or spiral-shank siding nails CLASS
furring / rainscreen strapping CLASS (coastal CMHC — not Utah/Fontana habit)
typical_duration_sfr: CMHC Ch2: one to two weeks for exterior finishes — Canadian sample. No lag days invented.
when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit. Stucco / masonry / EIFS are documented alts.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Siding before WRB. Nailing vinyl tight so it cannot move. Copying CMHC 8 in grade as Utah habit. Selling EIFS as first-touch. Fontana WUI notes only on foothills — do not copy onto Wasatch/Logan.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They hang siding. What they skip is 1-1/2 in above the lap (so the course below can move), Type 15 felt first, and vinyl nails in the slot centers.
permit_gate: cladding type should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: WUI foothills Fontana only — do not copy onto Wasatch/Logan. Confirm AHJ.
risk_if_swapped_late: Swapping wood siding for masonry after the foundation is in moves the brick ledge. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: Wrap first. Then siding. One nail per stud on bevel, 1 inch lap, nail above the lap so the board under it can move. Hot-dipped nails. Keep siding off the dirt (AF&PA says 6 inches). Vinyl nails sit in the slot, not slammed home.
spanish_summary: Primero el wrap. Luego el siding. Un clavo por stud en bisel, traslape de 1 pulgada, clavo arriba del traslape. Clavos galvanizados. Fuera de la tierra (AF&PA 6 pulgadas). Vinilo: clavo en la ranura, no apretado.

CMHC Ch13 Exterior Cladding — lumber/vinyl/hardboard; Fig 109–112
confidence_notes: AF&PA nail length and 1-nail-per-stud high (US). CMHC 1 in penetration and vinyl slot-nail high but Canadian. Grade 6 in vs 8 in kept as labeled variants. No crew.
